headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: PaddleOCR can process documents/images while Prefect can orchestrate workflows and egress broadly, creating a default path from sensitive inputs into downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not established. However, PaddleOCR can emit parsed document text/images and Prefect can orchestrate downstream workflows; if operators bridge them via files or APIs, attacker-controlled document content could be treated as instructions. This is an inferred, not documented, interaction, so severity stays low.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is copied into a Prefect task input without sanitization
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Add a manual review step before any OCR text is used as workflow input
Restrict Prefect tasks to structured fields only
Disable automatic execution of OCR-derived instructions
Use a separate staging folder for untrusted documents
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all OCR outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images, while Prefect has broad network egress. If they share a workspace or workflow, sensitive document contents can flow from A into B and then out over networked tasks. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default automation setups, though not directly evidenced, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF documents or images processed by PaddleOCR are passed into Prefect tasks
IF Prefect tasks transmit task inputs or logs to external services
mitigations: Limit Prefect task inputs to redacted metadata
Store OCR outputs in a restricted folder
Turn off verbose task logging for document payloads
Review outbound destinations before enabling the flow
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: PaddleOCR has allowlisted egress and browser use, while Prefect has broad egress and API calls. The profiles do not show shared writable storage, git state, or overlapping mutable scopes, so a direct write conflict is not supported. Any conflict would require extra orchestration not shown here.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory or database
IF Prefect orchestrates concurrent writes from OCR and downstream tasks
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Keep Prefect tasks read-only where possible
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR produces extracted document content, and Prefect is an orchestration layer that can act on task outputs. If Prefect treats OCR output as authoritative, extraction errors can cascade into automated downstream actions. The interaction is inferred from the profiles, not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Prefect uses PaddleOCR output as a trigger or decision input
IF no verification step checks OCR confidence or source documents
mitigations: Require human approval for high-impact tasks
Pass OCR confidence scores downstream
Compare OCR output against source snippets
Add validation rules before orchestration
requires-engineering: implement exception handling for low-confidence parses

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images, while Prefect touches workflow metadata. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to possible policy gaps if sensitive documents are routed through Prefect logs or external APIs. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined workflow.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through Prefect-managed workflows
IF Prefect retains logs containing OCR-derived content longer than policy allows
mitigations: Exclude document text from workflow logs
Set short retention on Prefect artifacts
Route regulated data through a compliant storage tier
Review data residency settings before deployment
requires-engineering: map data flows to policy controls
